subject: Math
prompt:
$$6x-9y=36$$

A system of two linear equations in the xy-plane has no solution. One of the equations is shown above. Which equation could be the other equation in the system?
explanation: For a system to have no solution, the lines must be parallel but distinct (same slope, different y-intercepts). Dividing the given equation $6x-9y=36$ by $3$ yields $2x-3y=12$. Choice D shows $2x-3y=15$, which has the same left side as the simplified given equation but a different constant term. This means both equations have the same slope but different y-intercepts, creating parallel distinct lines with no solution.
